contents.name: CHAPTER 8. RAM PROGRAMS, TURING MACHINES, AND CHURCH'S THESIS
Theorem 8.2. A partial function is computable by a RAM program iff it is Turing-computable.
Theorem 8.3. A relation is accepted by a RAM program iff it is accepted by some Turing machine.
CHAPTER 9. UNIVERSAL RAM PROGRAMS AND THE HALTING PROBLEM
Proposition 9.5. For the indexing of RAM programs defined earlier, there is a universal partial computable function phi_univ.
The program UNIV computing phi_univ can be viewed as an interpreter for RAM programs. We can view the RAM model as a stored program computer.
